<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par116 />''God''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=2|verse=15}}; with an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=127|verse=2}}; with a noun-suffix (which, according to {{GHGpar|33|c}}, also represents a genitive), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־מֹֽצְאִי|translate=whosoever findeth me}} (prop. my finder; cf. {{GHGheb|text=עֹשִׂי|translate=my maker}}); 12:3 {{GHGheb|text=מְבָֽרֲכֶ֫יךָ|translate=that bless thee}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְקַלֶּלְךָ|translate=that curseth thee}} (but read either {{GHGheb|text=מְקַלְלֶ֫יךָ}}, or {{GHGheb|text=מְבָֽרֶכְךָ}} in the preceding clause); 27:29, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=63|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=49}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=22}} read {{GHGheb|text=מְשָֽׁרְתִים אֹתִי}}.<ref>When, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=19}}, the participle with the noun-suffix {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֹשׂוֹ|translate=he that made him}}, also has the article (cf. {{GHGpar|127|i}}), the anomaly is difficult to understand, since a word determined by a genitive does not admit of being determined by the article.—No less remarkable is the use of the constr. st. of the participle before the accusative in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=33|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=מְשָֽׁרְתֵי אֹתִי|translate=that minister unto me}} (for which there is {{GHGheb|text=מְשָֽׁרְתַי}} in verse 21). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=13}} an accusative of the product follows the genitive of the object, {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֵׂה שַׁחַר עֵיפָה|translate=maker of the morning into darkness}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵת מֽוֹלִכֵךְ}} is supposed to mean ''at the time when he led thee''; perhaps the perfect ({{GHGheb|text=הוֹל׳}}) should be read as in 6:15. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=27|verse=34}}, the ancient versions read {{GHGheb|text=עַתָּ}}({{GHGheb|text=ה}}) {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁבַּרְתְּ|translate=now thou art broken}}, instead of the difficult {{GHGheb|text=עֵת נִשְׁבֶּ֫רֶת}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=40}} read {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֶׂה}} before {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫נָּה וָהֵ֫נָּה}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|h}}
Rem. To the class of objective genitives belong also specifications of place after the participles {{GHGheb|text=בָּא|translate=iniens}} and {{GHGheb|text=יֹצֵא|translate=egrediens}}, since the verbs {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}, in the sense of ''ingredi, egredi'', can be directly connected with an accusative; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=10}}, 18 {{GHGheb|text=בָּאֵי שַׁ֫עַר עִירוֹ|translate=that went in at the gate of his city}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=4}}; after {{GHGheb|text=יֹֽצְאֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=26|hidebook=1}}, &c.—In poetic language the participle in the construct state may be connected not only with a genitive of the object, but also with any other specifications (especially of space) which otherwise can only be made to depend on the verb in question by means of a preposition; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=18}}, and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=יֽוֹרְדֵי־בוֹר|translate=they that go down into the pit}} (the grave); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=88|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁכְבֵי קֶ֫בֶר|translate=that lie in the grave}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=24}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=17}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=5}}, 7, 9 ''those that came in'' (or ''went out'') ''on the sabbath'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=5|verse=18}}, &c.; instead of the construction with {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=20}} (''those who turn from transgression''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=8}} (cf. {{GHGpar|72|p}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|i}}
These genitives of nearer definition appear also in the form of a noun-suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=40}}, 49 {{GHGheb|text=קָמַי}} (for {{GHGheb|text=קָמִים עָלַי}}) ''that rise up against me''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=32|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=27}} {{GHGheb|text=שָׁבֶ֫יהָ|translate=her converts}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=53|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=חֹנָךְ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=2|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־בָּאֶ֫יהָ|translate=all that go unto her}}; the construction is especially bold in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־צֹבֶ֫יהָ וּמְצֹֽדָתָהּ|translate=all that fight against her and her stronghold}} (for {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־הַצֹּֽבְאִים עָלֶ֫יהָ וְעַל־מ׳}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=9}} even with a participle Poʿal, {{GHGheb|text=מְהֽוֹלָלַי|translate=they that are mad against me}} (?), but read perhaps with Olshausen {{GHGheb|text=מְחֽוֹלְלַי|translate=who pierce me}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=30}} ''as a terebinth'' {{GHGheb|text=נֹבֶ֫לֶת עָלֶ֫הָ|translate=fading as regards its leaf}}, it remains doubtful whether {{GHGheb|text=נֹבֶ֫לֶת}} is in the absolute state, and consequently {{GHGheb|text=עָלֶ֫הָ}} in the accusative, or whether it is to be regarded as construct state, and {{GHGheb|text=עָלֶ֫הָ}} as the genitive. In the latter case it would be analogous to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=2}} (see ''k'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|k}}
'''4.''' The passive participles also may either be in the absolute state, and take the determining word in the accusative,<ref>On the proper force of this accusative when retained in the passive construction cf. below, {{GHGpar|117|cc}}, &c., and {{GHGpar|121|c}}, ''d''. So also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=12}} is to be understood, ''and the builders'' were {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ חַרְבּוֹ אֲסוּרִים עַל־מָתְנָיו|translate=girded every one with his sword on his side, and building}}.</ref> or may be connected<section end=par116 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
